q: Was the music in the first GTA real or made for the game?
a: Made for the game. All seven stations in GTA (1997) played original music by DMA Design's own musicians, credited to invented bands, and sound designer Colin Anderson treated avoiding licensed music as a core principle.

q: What were all the radio stations in GTA Vice City?
a: Nine: Wildstyle, Flash FM, Fever 105, V-Rock, Emotion 98.3, Wave 103 and Radio Espantoso for music, plus the talk stations K-Chat and VCPR. Lazlow hosts V-Rock; per Grand Theft Wiki, Toni (Maria Chambers) hosts Flash FM.

q: Is the GTA Vice City soundtrack on CD?
a: Yes. Epic Records and Sony Music released seven CDs in 2002, one per music station, each with the DJ chatter and fake ads. They sold for $13.98 each or $49.98 as a set (reported); the talk stations were never released.

q: Who voiced the DJs in GTA San Andreas?
a: Per GameSpot's 2004 launch coverage, Axl Rose hosts K-DST, George Clinton hosts Bounce FM, Chuck D hosts Playback FM, Michael Bivins hosts CSR, and Sly Dunbar and Robbie Shakespeare host K-Jah West. Julio G plays himself on Radio Los Santos.

Only a little. Per gta.wiki, five tracks were licensed, including Bula Matari's "Taxi Drivers" and two Flytronix tracks; the rest was written in-house. GTA 2's bigger change was adding DJs and satirical ads.

q: Is Phil Collins really in GTA Vice City Stories?
a: Yes. A computer-animated Phil Collins performs "In the Air Tonight" in the game, and one storyline has Victor Vance getting him safely to his concert. The song also plays on Emotion 98.3.

Lazlow is the radio host and writer behind much of early GTA talk radio: he hosted Chatterbox FM in GTA III and V-Rock in Vice City, and took over Entertaining America on San Andreas' WCTR. Wikipedia says he left Rockstar in 2020 after nearly 20 years.
